title: Many-Shot Regurgitation (MSR) Prompting

live_model.evidence: Sec 4.1: "We evaluated the verbatim regurgitation behavior of three language models: GPT-3.5 (engine: gpt-3.5-turbo-1106), GPT-4 (engine: gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09)..."; Table 1 row GPT-4/Wikipedia.

prompt.location: Sec. 2 (MSR construction described algorithmically: segments T1..Tn arranged as faux user/model conversation turns in a single prompt)
prompt.note: Method is fully specified but no verbatim prompt string is printed anywhere in the paper.

claim.metric: Cliff's delta, verbatim-match-length distribution Dpre vs Dpost, Wikipedia
claim.location: Table 1, row Wikipedia/GPT-4 (Cliff's Delta -0.828, KS distance 0.75, KW H 7.77, p=0.0053); ~600 Dpre + ~600 Dpost Wikipedia articles (Sec 4.1)

data.source: Wikipedia articles and OpenStax OER textbooks (curated pre/post training-cutoff); code at https://github.com/luffycodes/Many-Shot-Regurgitation-MIA

notes: MSR prompting is explicitly built on the many-shot jailbreaking technique (a single prompt simulating many fake conversation turns to force continuation) in order to elicit verbatim training-data regurgitation; this is a training-data-extraction/jailbreak-style manipulation of the model's guardrails, so we do not submit it to a commercial API even though the elicited content (Wikipedia/textbook text) is itself benign. Everything else about the record is otherwise clean: dated engine, role S, numeric claim with n, public data.
